title: Lean 4 sources for the near-tight lonely runner papers and the six-speed classification
description: Lean 4 modules (Mathlib, Lean 4.30.0), 1,353 of them, that the three papers on near-tight sets of lonely runner speeds cite as their Lean evidence, as an overlay on the five-speed archive (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24443755). Includes the classification of six distinct positive integers with ML <= 1/7 (TheoremA_unconditional) and saved axiom outputs. A clean-checkout build of the umbrella module LRSpectrumFull.Sext6.Gap.All (362 modules) was run with 0 failures and standard axioms only; the full Release closure was not rebuilt from a clean checkout. The Lean modules, programs and the first drafts of the text were produced by an AI system (Claude, Anthropic) under the direction of Vico Bonfioli, who set the questions and directions; independent AI sessions reviewed them. The Lean kernel, not a human reader, checks the Lean proofs. Not peer reviewed. No proof of the lonely runner conjecture is claimed.
